title: Is Gas Cheaper Now Than Under Biden?

scenes.purpose: Open on the first half of the paradox: in January 2026 gas sat well under the Biden-era average.

visual.description: Two price tiles side by side: the Biden-era average on the left in neutral, January 2026 on the right landing in green on "well under".

chart.title: Regular gas, national monthly average
chart.note: Nominal dollars per gallon, not adjusted for inflation.

citations.label: EIA, U.S. regular gasoline, monthly average

scenes.direction: Cold open; the average tile is up first, the January tile punches in on "well under".
scenes.narration: In January 2026, a gallon of regular gas cost well under its average for Joe Biden's presidency.

scenes.purpose: Flip the paradox: by spring the same price was well over that average.

visual.description: Same two-tile layout; the January tile is replaced by May 2026, landing in red on "well over".

chart.title: Regular gas, national monthly average
chart.note: Nominal dollars per gallon, not adjusted for inflation.

citations.label: EIA, U.S. regular gasoline, monthly average

scenes.direction: Hard cut from sc01 so the swap of the right tile reads as the reversal.
scenes.narration: By spring, it cost well over it.

scenes.purpose: Pose the question the video answers.

visual.description: The question types on, large and centred; "now" holds and turns amber on "what you mean by now".
onScreenText: Is gas cheaper now than under Biden?

scenes.direction: Hold on the question through the second clause.
scenes.narration: So is gas cheaper now than under Biden? That depends on what you mean by now.

scenes.purpose: Give the cheaper-now claim in the president's own words.

visual.description: Quote card, text only: the two quoted phrases appear as spoken; "225" holds and turns amber.
onScreenText: "It was $4 and $5 for a gallon of gas"

citations.label: Donald Trump at a cabinet meeting, via WRAL
Donald Trump at a cabinet meeting, via WRAL

scenes.direction: Hard cut in; each line lands on its phrase.
scenes.narration: President Trump made the case at a cabinet meeting: "It was $4 and $5 for a gallon of gas", he said, "and now it's probably 225".

scenes.purpose: Give the opposite report from the spring.

visual.description: Quote card, text only, mirrored from sc04; "highest point" turns red as it is spoken.

citations.label: CBS News, spring 2026

scenes.direction: Wipe from the previous quote card; hold half a second.
scenes.narration: By this spring, CBS News was reporting pump prices "at their highest point since mid-2022".

scenes.purpose: Set the yardstick: the Biden-era average and its peak, from the EIA record.

visual.description: Two tiles build in turn as each figure is spoken: the Biden-era average, then the June 2022 peak in red. The source line "EIA, nominal dollars" sits under the title from s06.

chart.title: Regular gas under Biden, Feb 2021 to Jan 2025
chart.note: Nominal dollars per gallon, not adjusted for inflation.

citations.label: EIA, U.S. regular gasoline, monthly average

scenes.direction: Title in on s06; the average tile on "$3.46", the peak tile on "$4.93".
scenes.narration: Here is the record to check them against: the Energy Information Administration's national monthly average for regular gas, in dollars not adjusted for inflation. From February 2021 through January 2025, it came to $3.46 a gallon, with a peak of $4.93 in June 2022.

scenes.purpose: Check 2025 against the yardstick: below the average, level with the end of Biden's term, far above $2.25.

visual.description: Three tiles: December 2025 lands first on s08; then on s09 the Biden-era average and January 2025 (the last month of his term) join it, the last two close in size to show the level comparison.

chart.title: Regular gas, national monthly average
chart.note: Nominal dollars per gallon, not adjusted for inflation.

citations.label: EIA, U.S. regular gasoline, monthly average

scenes.direction: December tile on "$2.89"; the other two tiles on "Biden-era average" and "last months of his term".
scenes.narration: In 2025 the lowest month, December, came to $2.89, well above the president's guess. Every month of 2025 was below the Biden-era average, but about level with the last months of his term.

scenes.purpose: Show the spring jump in the weekly price.

visual.description: Two tiles: the first week of March in neutral, then mid-May slamming in red on "$4.50".

citations.label: EIA, U.S. regular gasoline, weekly average

scenes.direction: Camera punches on the second tile; hold half a second after.
scenes.narration: Then the weekly price jumped, from $3.02 in the first week of March 2026 to $4.50 by mid-May.

scenes.purpose: Give the news explanation for the jump in the reporters' own words.

visual.description: Two quote lines, text only, each appearing as spoken: MS NOW's line first, NBC News's beneath it; "the war in Iran" turns amber.
onScreenText: "up by well over a dollar since the war started"
"it's the war in Iran that's largely causing fuel prices to rise"

citations.label: MS NOW
NBC News

scenes.direction: Each line lands on its quotation; the citation under each line names its outlet.
scenes.narration: News reports tied the jump to the war with Iran: MS NOW said gas was "up by well over a dollar since the war started", and NBC News put it plainly: "it's the war in Iran that's largely causing fuel prices to rise".

scenes.purpose: Show crude oil jumping in the same month.

visual.description: Two tiles: February 2026 crude in neutral, March 2026 landing in red on "$91.38".

chart.title: West Texas Intermediate crude, monthly average

citations.label: EIA, WTI crude oil, monthly average

scenes.direction: Each tile on its figure.
scenes.narration: West Texas Intermediate crude oil jumped in the same month, from $64.51 a barrel in February to $91.38 in March.

scenes.purpose: Say what the price record can and cannot show about the cause.

visual.description: One line sets centred: "Cannot rule out other causes"; "other causes" underlines as it is spoken.

citations.label: EIA, U.S. regular gasoline, weekly average

scenes.direction: Line appears on "cannot rule out"; hold half a second.
scenes.narration: Those reports tie the rise to the war; the price record shows when prices jumped, but on its own it cannot rule out other causes.

scenes.purpose: Give the matching claim about crude in the president's own words.

visual.description: Quote card, text only; "higher under Biden" turns amber as it is spoken.
onScreenText: "Oil was higher under Biden than it is under Trump"

citations.label: Donald Trump, October 2026, via Right Side Broadcasting Network

scenes.direction: Hard cut in; hold after the quote.
scenes.narration: In October, President Trump made the same kind of claim about crude: "Oil was higher under Biden than it is under Trump".

scenes.purpose: Check the crude claim and give the gas price for the same month.

visual.description: Three tiles: September 2026 crude lands first, then the June 2022 crude peak beside it (higher), on "except March through July 2022"; on s16 the September 2026 gas tile joins in a separate colour, marked per gallon.

chart.title: Crude per barrel and gas per gallon
chart.note: WTI crude in dollars per barrel; regular gas in dollars per gallon; nominal.

citations.label: EIA, WTI crude oil, monthly average
EIA, U.S. regular gasoline, monthly average

scenes.direction: Crude tiles on s15, the gas tile on "Gas, meanwhile".
scenes.narration: In September, the latest month in the EIA's crude table, it averaged $97 a barrel, higher than in every month of Biden's term except March through July 2022. Gas, meanwhile, averaged $4.36 a gallon in September.

scenes.purpose: Show gas moving with crude under both presidents.

visual.description: Four tiles in two columns, gas on the left and crude on the right: the June 2022 pair lands on "both peaked in June 2022", the March 2026 pair on "both jumped in March 2026". A render may draw the pairs as a dumbbell.

chart.title: Gas and crude move together
chart.note: Moving together does not show what moved either price.

citations.label: EIA, U.S. regular gasoline, monthly average
EIA, WTI crude oil, monthly average

scenes.direction: Pairs land on their phrases; a short dip beat on "ended 2025 lower" between them.
scenes.narration: Put the lines side by side and the pump price has moved with crude under both presidents: both peaked in June 2022, both ended 2025 lower than they started it, and both jumped in March 2026.

scenes.purpose: Give the global-market view and its limit.

visual.description: Quote card, text only: the quoted phrase appears as spoken; "global market" turns amber; during the caveat the card dims slightly.

citations.label: Guest on PBS NewsHour

scenes.direction: Quote lands on its words; dim the card on "but prices moving together".
scenes.narration: That fits what a guest on PBS NewsHour said, that the pump price "is set in a global market"; but prices moving together cannot show that policy played no part, since policy can move crude itself.

scenes.purpose: Give the answer to the gas question: it depends on the month.

visual.description: Two lines build: "Through February 2026: yes" in green, then "Since March: no" in red.

citations.label: EIA, U.S. regular gasoline, monthly average

scenes.direction: Each line on its clause; hold one second after.
scenes.narration: So whether gas is cheaper than under Biden depends on the month: yes, against his term's average, through February 2026; no, in every month since March, though still short of that 2022 peak.

scenes.purpose: Turn from gas to prices overall.

visual.description: The question types on, centred.

scenes.direction: Wipe in from the previous scene; this opens the second half.
scenes.narration: But gas is one price among many. What about prices overall?

scenes.purpose: Give the prices-overall comparison in the channel's own words.

visual.description: Quote card, text only; "21%" holds and turns amber.

citations.label: Squirrelly Economics

scenes.direction: Hard cut in; hold after the quote.
scenes.narration: The channel Squirrelly Economics put the comparison this way: "Prices rose about 21% over Biden's 4 years".

scenes.purpose: Show the consumer price index totals for each term.

visual.description: Two lines build, one per sentence: Biden's term total first, then this term so far, smaller numbers in a second colour.

citations.label: BLS, consumer price index (CPI-U)

scenes.direction: Each line on its sentence.
scenes.narration: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' consumer price index agrees: it rose 21.4 percent from January 2021 to January 2025. From January 2025 to September 2026, the latest month, it rose 6.1 percent.

scenes.purpose: Name the flaw in comparing the totals.

visual.description: One line sets large; "still under way" turns amber.
onScreenText: A full term against one still under way

scenes.direction: Hold half a second after.
scenes.narration: But that sets a full term against one still under way, over a much shorter stretch.

scenes.purpose: Compare like with like: equally long stretches at each end of Biden's term.

visual.description: Two lines build: the start of Biden's term, then the end, each landing on its figure.

citations.label: BLS, consumer price index (CPI-U)

scenes.direction: First line on "at the start", second on "at the end".
scenes.narration: Over stretches as long as this one so far, at each end of Biden's term, prices rose 13.5 percent at the start, January 2021 to September 2022, and 4.5 percent at the end, May 2023 to January 2025.

scenes.purpose: Show the inflation rate climbing in the same months gas jumped.

visual.description: Two horizontal bars, February then September 2026, growing in as each figure is spoken; values printed at the bar ends.

citations.label: BLS, consumer price index (CPI-U)

scenes.direction: Each bar on its figure.
scenes.narration: And the count is still running: the year-on-year rate climbed from 2.4 percent in February 2026 to 3.7 percent in September, the same months gas jumped.

scenes.purpose: Give the answer to the prices question and its limit.

visual.description: Three lines build: "Slower than Biden's term as a whole" in green, "Faster than his last stretch" in red, then "Cause: not shown" in neutral.
onScreenText: Slower than Biden's term as a whole

citations.label: BLS, consumer price index (CPI-U)

scenes.direction: Each line on its clause; the third on "cannot say". Hold one second after.
scenes.narration: So prices have risen more slowly this term than across Biden's term as a whole, though faster than in his last stretch, and by a smaller margin than the totals suggest; and the index cannot say how much of either rise any president caused.

scenes.purpose: Tie both answers to the calendar.

visual.description: One line sets large; "calendar" holds and turns amber.
onScreenText: Both answers turned on the calendar

scenes.direction: Slow push in.
scenes.narration: Both answers turned on the calendar: which month counts as now, and how long a stretch you measure.

scenes.purpose: Leave the viewer the questions to ask.

visual.description: Three short lines build: "Compared with when?", "Over how long?", then "What did crude do?".

scenes.direction: Lines on their phrases; hold one second at the end before the fade.
scenes.narration: So when someone tells you prices are lower, ask: compared with when, and over how long? And when the pump price moves, check what crude oil did that month.
